question: Under the Transplantation of Human Organs and Tissues Act (THOTA) 1994 as amended in 2011, brain death for the purpose of deceased organ donation must be certified by how many doctors?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. A single doctor cannot certify brain death for transplantation purposes. THOTA requires a specific multi-doctor panel to prevent conflicts of interest and ensure diagnostic accuracy.

answers.text: Two doctors — the treating doctor and a neurologist/neurosurgeon

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. THOTA 1994 (amended 2011) requires four doctors to certify brain death for organ donation: a panel that includes the treating doctor, a neurologist or neurosurgeon, an anaesthesiologist or intensivist, and the medical officer in charge of the hospital.

answers.text: Four doctors including the treating doctor, a neurologist/neurosurgeon, an anaesthesiologist/intensivist, and the hospital medical officer

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. THOTA (amended 2011) mandates a four-doctor panel for brain death certification: the registered medical practitioner in charge of the patient, a neurologist or neurosurgeon (or in their absence, a surgeon or physician), an anaesthesiologist or intensivist, and the nominated medical officer of the hospital.

answers.text: Three doctors — a neurologist, an intensivist, and a transplant surgeon

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. The transplant surgeon is specifically excluded from the certification panel to prevent conflict of interest (the surgeon who will benefit from the organs cannot certify death). THOTA requires four specific categories of doctors.

overallFeedback.feedback: THOTA requires four doctors for brain death certification. The transplant surgeon is deliberately excluded to avoid conflict of interest. Two sets of brain death tests, performed 6 hours apart, must both be confirmed.

Correct. Four doctors must certify brain death under THOTA: treating doctor, neurologist/neurosurgeon, anaesthesiologist/intensivist, and hospital medical officer. Two separate sets of tests must be performed.
